prerequisites: Good knowledge of Machine Learning I
Good knowledge of Statistical Prediction Models

learning_outcomes.text: Know the main characteristics of Bayesian inference and its conceptual difference with classical inference.
Handle with ease the main Bayesian inference models based on conjugate distribution families.
Apply Bayesian models in networks and know the main elements of probabilistic graphical models.
Know and handle Bayesian regression and its main differences with the models seen in the Linear Models course.
Apply the above models in data science and engineering. Use MCMC models and Gibbs sampling.
Critically analyze the obtained results and predictions.

syllabus_topics: Prior, posterior and conjugate distributions. Credibility intervals. Bayesian hypothesis testing.
Markov chain Monte Carlo methods. Metropolis, Gibbs and Hamilton methods.
Bayesian networks. Bayesian filters. Probabilistic graphical models.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary and extraordinary calls, if a minimum score of 4.5 is achieved on the theoretical-practical exam (ExT), the final grade is calculated as 0.55 × ExT + 0.20 × EvC + 0.25 x I. Otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated score and 4.9 (fail). For differentiated evaluation, if a minimum score of 4.5 is achieved on the theoretical-practical exam (ExT), the final grade is calculated as 0.75 × ExT + 0.25 x I. Otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated score and 4.9 (fail). In case of doubt about authorship or unauthorized means, students may be asked for an oral defense.
